mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the foreign corporate shareholder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders and UBOs against the Canadian consolidated sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, and the EU/UK consolidated sanctions lists. PEP status must be disclosed in a certification; foreign PEPs are subject to enhanced continuous due diligence, independent source-of-funds verification, and senior management approval for any unusual ad-network payout routing. Pure publisher of lightweight ad-monetized games is classified as low AML risk but must not collect or transmit funds on behalf of third parties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre and NUANS Name Search (https://www.ic.gc.ca/app/scr/cc/CorporationsCanada)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name may be in English, French, or both. If a bilingual name is used, both versions must be conceptually equivalent and not confusing within the meaning of sections 10-12 CBCA. The legal element (Limited, Incorporated, Corporation, or accepted abbreviation) may be in either official language. Only Latin-alphabet characters are recorded; non-Latin script names must be transliterated and the transliteration is the operative corporate name. A NUANS report must show no confusingly similar existing federal/corporate name or registered trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Canada (if it implies federal agency status)
Benefit (unless the articles designate a benefit corporation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No extension is available for a NUANS-based name proposal; a new search report is required after 90 days. If the Director rejects the name, the applicant may file a Request for Reconsideration addressed to the Director, Corporations Canada, setting out why the name is not confusing, and attaching the refusal letter and a new NUANS report. For a final adverse decision, judicial review may be commenced in the Federal Court within 30 days of the written refusal. Alternatively, the incorporator may file articles with a different name or use an incorporated number name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted if provided by a licensed registered-office/corporate-service provider maintaining a physical street address in the designated province and accepting service of process during normal business hours. A post-office box or non-street virtual address is not acceptable. No industry-specific restriction applies to an ISIC 5820 hyper-casual mobile game publisher; however, the registered office must be a genuine service address and the company should maintain at least billing/ad-network contractual substance through physical corporate records available to the CRA.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; approximate 5% annual probability for a private, fully online hyper-casual game publisher. CRA or Corporations Canada will most often conduct documentary verification; unannounced physical inspection may occur only where books, records or registered office issues are identified as high-risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C., 1985, c. C-44, as amended – s. 5 (Articles of Incorporation), s. 6 (Contents of Articles), s. 14 (Certificate of Incorporation), s. 19 (Registered Office), ss. 101-106 (First Directors and Officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) together with Initial Registered Office Address and First Board of Directors (Form 4002)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA; shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine, and no escrow account is required for this low-risk digital publishing activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) The share subscriptions set forth in the Articles of Incorporation are accepted, and the directors are authorized to issue Class A common shares to the subscribers upon payment of the agreed consideration. (2) The registered office of the corporation is established at the address stated in the Articles, and the first director named in Form 4002 is confirmed as the person authorized for service of process. (3) The following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary. (4) The directors and officers are authorized to execute all agreements, banking resolutions, and regulatory filings necessary to complete federal incorporation and provincial extraprovincial registration. A certified copy of this resolution shall be placed in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Search and NUANS Reservation (Optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online portal (www.corporationscanada.ca) and approved NUANS search service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search through an approved service provider to confirm the proposed corporate name is distinguishable from existing names and trademarks. If a name-based incorporation is desired, file Form 4000 (Name Reservation Request) online or by mail to reserve the name for 90 days. Alternatively, proceed with a numbered company (e.g., '1234567 Canada Inc.') to avoid delay.
required_dossiers: Form 4000 Name Reservation Request (if reserving name)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an amended request with a revised name or use a numbered company name; no fee is forfeited if the reservation is withdrawn before filing of articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Online Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Initial Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (ISED) – Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form 4001 (Articles of Incorporation) and Form 4002 (Initial Registered Office Address and First Board of Directors) via the Corporations Canada online filing service. Specify the authorized share structure (e.g., unlimited Class A common shares) and provide the addresses of directors. Pay the C$200 filing fee electronically. Electronic filing produces a digitally-signed Certificate of Incorporation; paper filing is available but slower.
required_dossiers: Form 4002 Initial Registered Office Address and First Board of Directors
NUANS name search report (for name-based corporations)
Director consents or declarations if required by provincial policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the deficiency through the Online Filing Centre and resubmit; material errors in approved articles may be corrected by filing Articles of Amendment (Form 4004) with the applicable fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Organization of Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, Corporations Canada issues the Certificate of Incorporation under CBCA s. 14. The incorporators and first directors then hold an organizational meeting: adopt By-law No. 1, accept share subscriptions, issue share certificates, appoint officers, and open a corporate bank account. Maintain a statutory minute book at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A lost or damaged Certificate of Incorporation may be replaced by a certified copy obtained from Corporations Canada; defects in organizational minutes may be corrected by a subsequent directors' resolution passed retroactively where permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial corporate registries (e.g., ServiceOntario for Ontario; BC Corporate Registry; Alberta Corporate Registry; Registre des entreprises du Québec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where the federal corporation carries on business outside the province of its registered office, file an extra-provincial registration before commencing business in that province (e.g., Ontario Extra-Provincial Licence under the Ontario Business Corporations Act). Submit the certified federal Certificate of Incorporation and current Corporate Profile Report. Repeat for each province where offices or employees are located.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
Corporate Profile Report from Corporations Canada
Provincial extra-provincial registration form (e.g., Ontario Form 1)
NUANS report if required by the province
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the provincial registrar rejects filing, correct the recorded deficiencies and resubmit; where certified documents are insufficient, obtain an updated Corporate Profile Report or certificate of status from Corporations Canada.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Operating Administration Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO) and municipal business licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for a federal Business Number (BN) and applicable program accounts such as GST/HST (RT account) and payroll (RP account) via the BRO portal. Confirm municipal zoning and business licence requirements for the office premises (e.g., commercial lease or home office). Register for provincial workers' compensation coverage (e.g., WSIB in Ontario) where employees are hired.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and municipal zoning verification
Lease agreement or office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects or queries the BN application, contact CRA Business Enquiries to correct information; if municipal licensing is refused due to zoning, apply for a minor variance or relocate the administrative office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – ISIC 5820 (software publishing) is an office-based digital activity subject to no federal industrial licensing board; only municipal business licensing and provincial workplace regulations apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no statutory industrial operating permit is required for hyper-casual mobile game publishing in Canada.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC), with provincial environmental agencies applying respective EIA rules
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical industrial facility; the Impact Assessment Act (S.C. 2019, c. 28) does not apply to office-based software publishing, and no EIA registration or full report is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no regulated wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams. Office waste must be handled under municipal solid waste bylaws; electronic waste (defunct servers, computers) must be recycled under provincial e-waste programs (e.g., Ontario Resource Recovery and Circular Economy Act).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises must obtain fire safety certification under the National Fire Code of Canada and applicable provincial fire codes; structural load and occupancy-load inspections apply for leased premises. Employers must maintain workers' compensation coverage (e.g., WSIB in Ontario or provincial WCB), comply with applicable occupational health and safety acts covering fire exits, electrical safety, and ergonomic standards, and meet accessibility requirements (e.g., AODA in Ontario) where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); secured web portal: My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/canada-revenue-agency-online-services.html); Business Registration Online (BRO) for real-time Business Number and program account creation; non-resident filing through the CRA Non-Resident Tax program or a Canadian tax representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident corporation that will carry on business in Canada or remit GST/HST must first obtain a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA. Where the entity is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act or a provincial equivalent, the BN is issued at incorporation or extra-provincial registration. For a foreign entity with no Canadian incorporation, the standard procedure is to file Form RC1, 'Request for a Business Number and certain accounts', together with certified constitutional documents, foreign registration certificates, and completed authorization if a representative will file. The BN is then activated for separate program accounts: GST/HST, corporate income tax, import/export, and payroll. A non-resident supplier of digital services or intangible property may register for the simplified GST/HST reporting regime, using the same RC1 or the dedicated non-resident GST/HST registration portal, and must retain all support in English or French acceptable to the CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Canadian-resident business corporation is taxed as a separate taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act (Canada) on its worldwide taxable income. There is no federal C-corporation/S-corporation-style pass-through status for a business corporation. A corporation that is neither resident nor carrying on business in Canada remains subject to federal tax only in respect of proceeds of disposition of taxable Canadian property and resource income earned in Canada. A Canadian-controlled private corporation may access the small business deduction, while a private corporation may be subject to the refundable dividend tax on hand rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian equivalent of a US check-the-box election exists; corporate classification follows domestic corporate law and Income Tax Act article, with no elective transparency for business corporations. Statutory elections relevant to hybrid mismatch and intercompany arrangements include the offsetting adjustment election under ITA ss. 18.2(6) and 18.3(3) to neutralize double-counting relief when hybrid mismatch rules have denied a deduction, and elections regarding deemed residence of a corporation under the Canada-US tax treaty. Useful tax elections also include fiscal period election under s. 249.1 for a non-calendar year end, accelerated capital cost allowance elections where permitted, section 216 elections for non-residents with rental income from Canadian real estate, and the non-arm's length transfer pricing documentation election? No general entity-classification election is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.additional_notes: A corporation carrying on hyper-casual mobile game publishing with non-resident AppLovin and AdMob counterparties must ensure the BN is issued before the GST/HST return is filed and before import/export accounts are used; CRA may impose section 240(2) registration penalties for failure to register when required.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Canada in any single calendar quarter or in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold). Non-resident suppliers of digital services and intangible property to Canadian customers are required to register for GST/HST once the same CAD 30,000 threshold is exceeded; platform operators may be deemed to make the supply. A registrant is then required to collect and remit 5% federal GST, plus provincial HST component where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, government pre-clearance API, or digital stamping mandate exists at the federal level in Canada. CRA does not operate a continuous transaction control regime. Electronic invoices are acceptable if they preserve integrity, authenticity, and readability, and all books and records required by ETA s. 286 and ITA s. 230 must be retained for at least six years. Voluntary e-invoicing networks based on Peppol or EDI are permitted; CRA may request invoice-level data during audits but does not require pre-clearance or fiscal validation before issuance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.nexus_explanation: Indirect tax nexus in Canada is based on whether the corporation makes taxable supplies in Canada in the course of a commercial activity. For a Canadian corporation in the hyper-casual gaming space, GST/HST registration is normally mandatory as soon as Canadian-source taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 per quarter or every person with a permanent establishment in Canada must register. Supply of downloadable games to non-resident app stores may be zero-rated; revenues from AdMob or AppLovin ad monetization generally derive from services supplied to non-resident advertising intermediaries and may be zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident recipient who is not registered for GST/HST. The supplier retains the burden to prove that the place of supply is outside Canada.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act applies where the supply of exported goods, services, or intangible personal property is made in Canada and the destination/place-of-supply rules deem the supply to be outside Canada. Hyper-casual gaming software licensed or sold to non-resident publishers and app-store operators is zero-rated where the software is to be used wholly outside Canada and the Canadian supplier has obtained the non-resident recipient's name, address, country of residence, and GST/HST registration status (if any). For services such as ad inventory mediation, performance marketing, and backend game support supplied to a non-resident advertiser or platform, zero-rating is available if the recipient is not a GST/HST registrant and the supply is not in respect of Canadian real estate or goods situated in Canada. For physical promotional merchandise exported from Canada, zero-rating requires export to be completed by the supplier within a reasonable time and documentary proof of export. The supplier must obtain the underlying transactional evidence before filing the net tax remittance in which the zero-rated supply is reported.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / B13 Canada Customs Coding Form filed with the Canada Border Services Agency where goods are exported
Commercial invoice, packing list, and complete product/game service description
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing foreign destination and export from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/FX credit advice evidencing settlement in foreign currency from the non-resident counterparty
Non-resident status evidence and GST/HST registration status of the recipient, including contracts, purchase orders, and end-user licence agreements
Export shipment records, customs broker acknowledgements, and internal shipping/dispatch logs retained in the CRA books-and-records file
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may audit zero-rating claims by testing place-of-supply, non-resident status, and the documentary trail for consideration received. Where a supply is found not to be zero-rated, the supplier is assessed for uncollected GST/HST, plus daily compound arrears interest from the date the return was due. The supplier may also lose previously claimed input tax credits or refunds. Civil penalties under the Excise Tax Act apply to false statements and omissions; a gross negligence scenario can attract a penalty, while conviction for wilful evasion can give rise to fines of up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and, in serious cases, imprisonment. CRA's normal reassessment period is four years, but misrepresentation, fraud, or wilful default removes the limitation period and permits retrospective clawback without time limit. Export zero-rating claims should be retainable for six years from the end of the reporting period, with augmented records when cross-border technology transactions are involved.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) with foreign-exchange administration exercised through the Minister of Finance, the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act; prudential supervision of banking counterparties rests with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), and AML/CFT supervision is administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully liberalized, free-floating FX regime with no exchange-control licensing, no capital-account approval gates, and no current-account restrictions. The Canadian dollar (CAD) is freely convertible into all major reserve currencies; foreign-currency deposit accounts (notably USD) are permissible both domestically and offshore. Profit remittance in the form of dividends and royalties faces no FX obstacle; the only frictional costs are Canadian Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, typically reduced to 5% for dividends and 0-10% for royalties under an applicable income tax treaty such as the Canada-US Treaty), Part I corporate tax clearance, and CRA informational filings (T5, T106, T1134/T1135). Directors and treasury managers should document the tax-residency of the ultimate beneficial owner of each receiving entity to ensure treaty-dependent withholding relief is correctly applied and that no deemed-dividend treatment arises on subordinated shareholder loans.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline on export proceeds or other foreign-currency receipts, including ad-network payouts received from AdMob and AppLovin. Exporters may maintain foreign-currency receivables offshore indefinitely; however, all worldwide income of a Canadian tax resident must be reported in CAD annually at the Bank of Canada noon exchange rate. If aggregate specified foreign property (including foreign bank accounts, foreign securities, and qualifying foreign receivables) exceeds CAD 100,000 in the year, Form T1135 must be filed, and controlled foreign affiliate holdings may trigger T1134 filings. No CAD conversion is compelled even when funds are later repatriated to a domestic operating account.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — admissible strictly as an ancillary collection/disbursement rail, never as the primary treasury account. Offshore digital EMIs are not chartered banks, are not prudentially regulated by OSFI, and carry no CDIC deposit insurance. A Canadian entity may use such providers for fast receipt of ad-network settlements, but the entity remains responsible for its own Part XIII / GST/HST / income-tax obligations and must keep the EMI float immaterial (recommended cap: CAD 50,000 aggregate, swept to a Schedule I bank within 24 hours). Any EMI that solicits Canadian business must itself be FINTRAC-registered as a money service business (MSB) and must meet Canadian AML obligations; the corporate treasury team should nonetheless treat EMI virtual-IBAN transactions as pass-through rather than revenue evidence, reconciling each EMI credit to the underlying AdMob/AppLovin payout statement. Legal constraint: a Canadian Business Corporation cannot use an unregistered foreign MSB as its registered bank, and auditors may require list of bank accounts to include EMI custody balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance at a Canadian branch is the default and the commercially prudent baseline: at least one authorized signatory or director must appear with original ID, notarized corporate documents, and a certified copy of the federal/extra-provincial registration. Several Schedule I banks (notably RBC and TD) offer remote/video onboarding for simple Canadian-controlled federal corporations, but non-resident directors face enhanced scrutiny: remote opening requires notarized certificates of good standing, banker's references, and a legal opinion confirming the CBCA director-residency requirement. Under the Canada Business Corporations Act, at least 25% of directors must be resident Canadians (or at least one director if the board has fewer than four directors); a fully foreign board is therefore impermissible for a CA_FED entity. Banks commonly insist that the Canadian-resident director or an appointed power-of-attorney holder co-sign the account. Practical mandate: schedule branch interviews for the Canadian-resident director and one foreign director, bring certified translations of all foreign-issued IDs, and complete the bank's corporate KYC form on the same day as the board resolution appointing banking authorities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: nominee shareholders, layered intermediate holding entities, or non-resident directors with no verifiable connection to Canada or to the operating business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Unredacted passports or national IDs for all directors and every shareholder holding 10% or more; federal and provincial corporate registry abstracts; complete organizational chart from UBO to signatory; CBCA Register of Individuals with Significant Control; board resolution confirming no nominee arrangements; Canadian legal opinion confirming CBCA s. 105(3) residency compliance and identifying all material registrants.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-model mismatch: high-volume, near-identical inbound credits from foreign ad networks (AdMob/AppLovin payout batches) flagged as unusual cash-equivalent or money-laundering flow patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed ad-network commercial agreements with Google Ireland Limited / Google LLC and AppLovin; trailing 12-month platform payout reports; monetization dashboard snapshots; revenue-recognition policy under ASC 606 / IFRS 15; sample app-store annd attribution metrics showing active global user base; monthly management accounts tying platform credits to accrued revenue; a written treasury memo explaining batch settlement cadence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth gap on the initial capital injection: incoming shareholder funds not matched to verifiable economic substance or prior business track record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized share-subscription agreement and board minutes authorizing issuance of shares; parent-company audited or reviewed financial statements; bank reference letters from the remitting bank; tax clearance certificates from the remitting jurisdiction; personal net-worth statement of the funding UBO if the injection is a gift or below fair value; source-of-funds declaration in the bank's prescribed form; CRA reference number for any foreign tax clearance received.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-rail interposition: funds arriving via digital EMI virtual IBANs, third-party gaming aggregators, or pass-through platforms rather than direct SWIFT credits from the contractual ad network.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contract chain evidencing each interposed settlement provider; EMI account statements in the entity's name; reconciliation workbook matching AdMob/AppLovin dashboard net payout to each bank or EMI credit, signed by the CFO; confirmation from the intermediary that no crypto conversion or tokenization occurs; schedule of all EMI and bank accounts held globally; a written internal treasury policy committing to direct SWIFT settlement to the preferred Schedule I bank wherever operationally possible.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid fund-velocity pattern: funds received from ad networks and disbursed within days to offshore contractors, game developers, or design agencies, creating a lending-like or invoice-factoring impression.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed outsourcing and licensing agreements with defined deliverables and milestone schedules; vendor KYC pack (beneficiary ID, bank details, jurisdiction proof); pro-forma invoices and milestone acceptance certificates; cash-flow forecast shared with the relationship manager; payment-run calendar demonstrating that disbursements lag AdMob/AppLovin confirmations by at least 2 business days; signed representation that funds are not used for third-party onward payment or virtual-asset activities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity injections from a non-resident parent or financing shareholder: transmit via SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 pain.001 if initiated via the bank's file-based channel) with remittance-information field coded as 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION – CAPITAL INJECTION – [Legal Entity Name]', and pre-notify the relationship manager with the name and jurisdiction of the remitter, the economic purpose, and the source-of-funds bundle. The bank routing must direct funds to a separately designated Capital Escrow / Share-Proceeds account so that operating cash is not commingled with contributed capital. All injections must be reconciled to the CBCA-required board resolution and the shareholder register; proceeds should be booked as stated capital (share premium if applicable), not as loans, unless a formal subordinated loan agreement is executed to avoid deemed-dividend treatment under Part XIII and to preserve the reserve-deficiency analysis for CRA. The Investment Canada Act must be assessed: for WTO-source non-cultural investors, notifiable review triggers on enterprise-value thresholds (CDN 1.045B+ for 2021 review thresholds, indexed and periodically adjusted); for cultural businesses such as broadcast or film, lower thresholds apply — although ISIC 5820 software publishing is generally non-cultural, the full game value chain should be validated by counsel before closing. Foreign reporting forms T1134/T1135 must be monitored where the parent or foreign shareholder creates specified foreign property in excess of CAD 100,000. Treasury should retain for each injection: subscription agreement, board minutes, remitter bank confirmation, foreign tax clearance if available, and a funds-flow diagram.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail for cross-border trade payments is SWIFT MT103 via the bank's secure file-upload or API channel, using the entity's standard credit line and pre-agreed purpose/beneficiary coding; recurring USD vendor and royalty payments should be consolidated into daily batches using pain.001 payment-initiation messages, with each payment carrying the underlying contract reference and tax withholding indicator. Domestic Canadian disbursements (contractors, hosting, payroll, HST remittances) settle over the Canadian EFT/ACH and LVTS wire systems; commercial letters of credit are not an appropriate rail for purchasing services or licensing intangibles in the hyper-casual games vertical, but may be used only where a major licensor or ad-tech partner demands documentary assurance — in such cases a standby LC or bank guarantee is the more standard alternative. For royalty and license-tuition outflows, the disbursing bank must receive (i) a valid non-resident withholding certificate or treaty-reduction documentation, (ii) the licensing agreement, and (iii) the royalty calculation workbook, so that bank-side OFAC, sanctions, and SOF checks are cleared before release. AdMob and AppLovin collection handling is reversed: the entity should instruct the ad networks to ACH/SWIFT to the Schedule I operating account in USD with immediate same-day wash into CAD where the functional-currency cap is applied, or to the dual-currency USD account that is swept periodically under a board-approved FX hedge policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (up to 12-month terms, rollable) executed on bank master dealing terms for CAD/USD and CAD/EUR revenue sweeps
FX swaps (spot against future or same-day swap/rollover legs) for managing USD/CAD liquidity timing without changing the structural position
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (USD fixed/float vs CAD fixed/float) for medium-term balance-sheet hedging where the Cayman or Canadian holdco carries USD-denominated intercompany debt
Vanilla FX options (call/put) and zero-cost collars on CAD/USD for hedging probabilistic ad-network revenue, subject to a board-approved hedging policy

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) solely for restricted or non-convertible emerging-market contractor currencies (e.g., certain LATAM/SEA/CE non-fully-convertible settlements); CAD itself is freely deliverable so NDFs on CAD/USD are not necessary or standard

Spot execution with bilateral credit lines and limit/stop orders via the bank's dealing desk; no algorithmic or high-frequency FX trading, and no crypto-backed hedging instruments permitted under the treasury mandate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation (CBCA s. 263)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late fee is prescribed; failure to file for two consecutive years may lead to administrative dissolution by the Director after issuance of a notice of default (CBCA s. 212). Directors and officers may also be liable for offences under the CBCA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each taxation year (Income Tax Act s. 150)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of the unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month of default, up to 12 months; repeated failure to file may trigger additional higher penalties. Interest accrues on unpaid amounts under s. 161 to 163 of the Income Tax Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based statutory audit requirement under the CBCA for non-distributing (private) corporations. An audit is mandatory if the corporation is a distributing (public) corporation, if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares or the Director require an audit, or if a regulator/lender imposes one. Otherwise, shareholders may waive the appointment of an auditor by unanimous resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS for private corporations, as permitted by the CPA Canada Handbook.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the CBCA, share transfers and changes in significant control must be recorded in the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register) within 15 days of the change. No separate annual UBO confirmation is filed with Corporations Canada; the federal Annual Return does not request shareholder-level UBO details. The ISC Register and Register of Members must be maintained on-site and be accessible as required by the CBCA.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% – federal general corporate income tax rate (38% basic federal rate less 10% provincial abatement and 13% general rate reduction); provincial corporate tax is imposed separately (e.g., 12% Ontario), outside the CA_FED jurisdictional limit.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction: effective 9% federal rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income for Canadian-Controlled Private Corporations (CCPCs); Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) Investment Tax Credit: 35% refundable for CCPCs on qualified current/development expenditures up to the CAD 3 million expenditure limit (15% non-refundable base credit otherwise); full deduction of expenditures on qualifying R&D salaries, materials, and overhead; accelerated capital cost allowance provisions for zero-emission technology assets (not typically applicable), and deductibility of deductible tax-exempt? Not applicable.
